samples.question: The black square in the middle of this picture is a hub. Exactly one grey wire touches each of its four sides - top, right, bottom and left - and each of those four wires runs to one of the four coloured squares near the edge of the picture: green, red, blue and orange. All the wires are drawn in the same grey with the same thickness, and wires often cross one another; where two wires cross, each one carries straight on through the crossing and neither one turns there. A wire turns only where it visibly ends its straight run and bends. First follow the wire that ends at the green square back to the hub and note which side of the hub it touches. Then move one side clockwise around the hub, where clockwise means top side, then right side, then bottom side, then left side, and back to top. Now follow the wire touching that next side out to its coloured square. Which coloured square does that wire end at? Answer red, blue or orange.
